config.title: isolation and stacking

intro.title: isolation and stacking
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage with overlapping colored boxes to visually explore how CSS controls element layering. You will learn the core concepts of stacking context and the isolation property, which determine how elements are layered on top of each other. The main technologies involved are CSS properties like z-index, position, and the newer isolation property. By the end, you'll understand how to manage and predict the stacking order of elements in your layouts.
intro.usecase: Isolation and stacking are essential for managing overlapping UI elements in modern web applications. Developers use these techniques when creating modal dialogs that must appear above all other content, dropdown menus that shouldn't be clipped by parent containers, or tooltips that need to float above complex layouts. In dashboard interfaces with multiple panels and widgets, isolation prevents z-index conflicts between components from different parts of the application. These concepts are particularly valuable when building design systems where components must maintain visual integrity regardless of where they're placed in the DOM hierarchy.

objectives: Apply the isolation property to create independent stacking contexts
Configure stacking order using z-index within isolated containers
Construct layered interfaces by manipulating stacking contexts
Implement isolation to prevent z-index conflicts between components
Control element visibility through stacking context management
Integrate isolation with positioning properties for predictable layering
Render complex UI patterns by combining multiple stacking contexts

steps.title: Create the HTML structure for stacking demonstration
steps.instruction: Create a simple HTML file with three div elements that will be used to demonstrate stacking contexts. Add three div elements with the class names 'box1', 'box2', and 'box3' inside a container div with class 'stack-container'.
steps.hint: Start with a basic HTML structure and add the container and three boxes as described. Each div should have a unique class for later styling.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a complete HTML file with three div elements ready for CSS styling to demonstrate stacking contexts.
successCriteria: The HTML file contains a div with class 'stack-container' and three child divs with classes 'box1', 'box2', and 'box3'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have exactly three div elements with the correct class names inside the container.
steps.feedbackWrong: Please create the HTML structure as described. You need a container div with three child divs, each with unique class names.

steps.title: Add basic styling to see the elements
steps.instruction: Open the styles.css file and add CSS rules to give the .stack-container and .box1, .box2, .box3 classes basic styling: set dimensions (width and height), background colors, and basic positioning.
steps.hint: Start by targeting the .stack-container class to set its dimensions and position. Then style each box individually with different background colors and sizes.

/* Add your CSS rules here */
/* Style .stack-container, .box1, .box2, .box3 */
steps.expectedOutcome: The three boxes will become visible with distinct colors and sizes, positioned within the container.
successCriteria: The CSS file contains rules for .stack-container with width/height and position, and each .box class has width, height, background-color, and position properties defined.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but make sure all required properties (width, height, background-color, position) are defined for each element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS doesn't include the necessary styling rules. Review the instruction and add properties for the container and boxes.

steps.title: Introduce the z-index property
steps.instruction: Add the z-index property to .box1, .box2, and .box3 with different values to control their stacking order.
steps.hint: Use z-index: 1; for .box1, z-index: 2; for .box2, and z-index: 3; for .box3. This will make box3 appear on top.
steps.expectedOutcome: The boxes will have different z-index values applied, changing their stacking order so box3 appears on top, then box2, then box1.
successCriteria: All three boxes (.box1, .box2, .box3) have z-index properties with distinct values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some z-index properties, but make sure all three boxes have distinct z-index values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The z-index properties are missing or incorrect. Add z-index to each box with different values.

steps.title: Create a stacking context with position
steps.instruction: Add a new CSS rule for a class named .stack-context that sets position: relative to create a new stacking context.
steps.hint: Use the position property with the value relative. This will make the element establish its own stacking context separate from the root.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS rule for .stack-context is added with position: relative, demonstrating how positioned elements create stacking contexts.
successCriteria: The .stack-context rule exists and includes position: relative.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the .stack-context rule includes position: relative. Check your syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .stack-context rule is missing or doesn't have position: relative. Remember, positioned elements (relative, absolute, fixed, sticky) create stacking contexts.

steps.title: Demonstrate isolation with isolation: isolate
steps.instruction: Add a new CSS rule for a class named .isolated-box that uses the isolation property set to 'isolate'.
steps.hint: The isolation property creates a new stacking context. Use the syntax: isolation: isolate;
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a new CSS rule that demonstrates how isolation creates a new stacking context separate from the parent.
successCriteria: The .isolated-box rule is defined with isolation: isolate;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've defined the .isolated-box class with isolation: isolate;
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule for .isolated-box is missing or incorrect. Remember to use isolation: isolate; to create a new stacking context.

steps.title: Show how isolation prevents z-index interference
steps.instruction: Add a child element inside the .isolated-box div in your HTML structure (not shown in the CSS) and style it with a high z-index to test if it can appear above elements outside the isolated stacking context.
steps.hint: You'll need to add a new CSS rule for a child element (e.g., .isolated-child) with position, z-index, and styling. The HTML structure already has a div with class 'isolated-box' from earlier steps.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a new CSS rule for a child element inside the isolated box, with a high z-index, to demonstrate that isolation prevents it from interfering with z-index of elements outside its stacking context.
successCriteria: A CSS rule for .isolated-child is added with position: absolute, a z-index value (e.g., 999), and styling properties like background-color, width, and height.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but make sure to include position: absolute and a z-index value for the .isolated-child rule to properly test isolation effects.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule for .isolated-child is missing or incomplete. Ensure you add a rule with position, z-index, and styling to demonstrate isolation's effect on stacking.

steps.title: Compare isolation with other stacking context creators
steps.instruction: Create a new CSS rule for a class named .opacity-context that creates a stacking context using opacity less than 1.
steps.hint: Use the opacity property with a value between 0 and 1 (like 0.99) to create a stacking context.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS rule that creates a stacking context using the opacity property.
successCriteria: The .opacity-context rule exists with opacity property set to a value less than 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your .opacity-context rule has opacity set to a value less than 1 (like 0.99).
steps.feedbackWrong: The .opacity-context rule should use opacity with a value less than 1 to create a stacking context.

steps.title: Demonstrate stacking order within a context
steps.instruction: Add two child elements inside the .isolated-box stacking context and control their stacking order with z-index.
steps.hint: Create two new CSS rules for child elements inside .isolated-box, give them different z-index values, and position them to overlap.
steps.expectedOutcome: Two child elements are defined within the .isolated-box stacking context, each with a different z-index value to demonstrate internal stacking order.
successCriteria: Two CSS rules for child elements inside .isolated-box are added, each with position: absolute, different z-index values, and overlapping positioning.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some child elements, but make sure both have position: absolute, different z-index values, and are positioned to overlap within .isolated-box.
steps.feedbackWrong: The child elements are not properly defined. Ensure you create two CSS rules for elements inside .isolated-box with absolute positioning and different z-index values.

steps.title: Show real-world use case for isolation
steps.instruction: Create a modal overlay scenario by adding a .modal class with high z-index and isolation: isolate to prevent conflicts with page content.
steps.hint: Define a .modal class with position: fixed, full viewport coverage, a high z-index like 1000, and isolation: isolate.
steps.expectedOutcome: A modal overlay class is defined with isolation to demonstrate solving common z-index conflicts in real layouts.
successCriteria: The .modal class includes position: fixed, full viewport coverage (top:0, left:0, width:100%, height:100%), a high z-index (e.g., 1000), and isolation: isolate.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but ensure the .modal class has all required properties: position: fixed, full viewport coverage, a high z-index, and isolation: isolate.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .modal class is missing or incomplete. Review the instruction to create a modal overlay with isolation.

steps.title: Review and test the complete stacking behavior
steps.instruction: Add a final test rule that changes the z-index of .box2 to 100 and observe how it interacts with the isolated elements
steps.hint: Create a new CSS rule targeting .box2 and set its z-index property to a high value like 100
steps.expectedOutcome: The green box (.box2) will appear above other non-isolated boxes but won't interfere with isolated stacking contexts
successCriteria: A CSS rule for .box2 with z-index: 100 is added to test stacking behavior
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're targeting .box2 specifically and setting z-index to 100.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating a CSS rule that targets .box2 and sets its z-index property to 100.
